# Detail Bug Report

https://app.detail.dev/org_d38a878f-9df9-4c4b-a96a-f5180b860085/bugs/bug_aafdfaf2-a64c-4e0c-a4be-93053a71b8ed

Introduced in d8da1796ded5deb5d49c66ef1cf759e3d95d146c by @LineIndent on Jul 17, 2026

# Summary
- **Context**: `components/ui/tabs.py` implements the library's Tabs component. `TabsTrigger.create` generates an id at Python build time and bakes that id and the trigger `value` into inline JavaScript (`rx.call_script`) that performs the active-tab highlight and root state update on click/mount.
- **Bug**: Because `create()` runs once at build time, every trigger rendered by an `rx.foreach` (or any single trigger instance rendered more than once) receives the *same* literal DOM id and the *same* literal JS, in which the per-item `value` Var has been interpolated as the Var's placeholder name — a meaningless string literal.
- **Actual vs. expected**: Each rendered tab should resolve to its own element and its own value when clicked; instead all copies share one id (`document.getElementById` returns only the first), and clicking any tab sets the root's `data-value` to a literal (e.g. `'item_rx_state_'`) that matches no trigger, so no trigger ever becomes active and no content panel is shown.
- **Impact**: Tabs built from a data list — the most common real-world pattern for a reusable UI component — fail silently: clicks do nothing visible, no tab is ever highlighted, and the root's value is set to a literal that matches no content panel. The failure mode also produces invalid HTML (duplicate element ids).

# Code with Bug
```python
# components/ui/tabs.py (TabsTrigger.create)
trigger_id = props.get("id") or f"tabs-trigger-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"   # <-- BUG 🔴 id baked once per create() call, shared by all rendered copies
props["id"] = trigger_id

js_on_click = f"""
(function() {{
    var trigger = document.getElementById('{trigger_id}');               # <-- BUG 🔴 duplicates mean this resolves to the first element, not the clicked one
    ...
    root.dataset.value = '{value}';                                      # <-- BUG 🔴 if value is a Var, this becomes a placeholder string literal
    root.querySelectorAll('[data-slot="tabs-trigger"]').forEach(function(t) {{
        ...
        t.setAttribute('data-active', t.getAttribute('data-value') === '{value}' ? 'true' : 'false');   # <-- BUG 🔴 compares against baked literal, never matches per-item data-value
    }});
}})()
"""
```

# Explanation
`TabsTrigger.create()` runs at template-build time, so any auto-generated `trigger_id` and any f-string interpolation of `value` are fixed once and reused for every runtime instance rendered from that same trigger (including `rx.foreach`.

This causes two independent breakages:
1) Duplicate DOM ids: `document.getElementById('{trigger_id}')` always returns the first element with that id, regardless of which tab was clicked.
2) Wrong tab value for foreach items: when `value` is a Var, `'{value}'` becomes the Var placeholder name (e.g. `'item_rx_state_'`) instead of the per-item runtime value. The trigger elements still render correct per-item `data-value` bindings, so the baked string literal never equals `t.getAttribute('data-value')`, preventing any trigger from becoming active and setting the root to a `data-value` that matches no content.

## Codebase Inconsistency
`components/ui/menu.py` documents the same “IDs baked once at template-build time inside rx.foreach” bug class for `MenuItem`, but `tabs.py` has no warning; additionally, for Tabs this isn’t fixable by passing an explicit `id` because the baked `'{value}'` literal still breaks foreach behavior.

# Recommended Fix
Stop keying behavior on a build-time id and baked value. In the click handler, resolve the trigger from the event target and read the runtime `data-value` attribute (and apply the same approach to the mount logic) so one script works for all rendered copies.

content.text:
I changed `components/ui/tabs.py` so tabs built with `rx.foreach` should now highlight the clicked tab. The full test suite passes (764 tests), but I didn't run it in a browser, so the foreach case itself is untested end to end.

I took "Gh108" to mean GitHub issue 108 (the Tabs `rx.foreach` bug) and fixed that.

- **Click:** the script no longer uses a build-time id or a baked `value`. It marks the clicked button from the runtime event, then reads that button's rendered `data-value`. Each foreach copy now resolves to its own element and value.
- **Mount:** the script sets `data-active` on every tab trigger by comparing its `data-value` to its tabs root's `data-value`. Because it now runs over all triggers on the page, it repeats work as each trigger mounts, but the result is the same.
- **Ids:** the generated `uuid` id is gone, so foreach triggers no longer produce duplicate ids.
- **Tests:** in `tests/test_tabs.py` I changed the helper and one assertion that read the click script. The script is now emitted as an escaped JS string, so the old text match no longer found it. I also removed the comment I'd added in `tabs.py`, because the repo's clean-code test forbids comments in components.

I haven't committed anything.
